title: FCC Approves Nexstar–TEGNA Merger as States Challenge Its Legality
description_short: FCC Approves Nexstar–TEGNA Merger as States Challenge Its Legality
description_medium: The linked TrumpFile report says the FCC and Justice Department approved the Nexstar–TEGNA merger on March 19, 2026, with six station divestitures and a combined reach of 54.5% of U.S. households. description_long: The linked TrumpFile report says the Federal Communications Commission and Justice Department approved Nexstar’s merger with TEGNA on March 19, 2026. It reports that the combined company would own 259 television stations and reach 54.5% of U.S. households after agreeing to divest six stations. The article says eight states sued, alleging that the transaction exceeded the 39% household-reach limit. Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser warned that consolidation could reduce media diversity and raise costs; Nexstar’s chair and CEO Perry Sook is also named. These details describe regulatory approval and a pending legal challenge, not a final judicial determination that the deal was illegal. The separate linked CBS story concerns a Disney/ABC licensing dispute and does not resolve the Nexstar–TEGNA case.
